The registered headline relation sign(EB/TB)=sign(x_h) (pr182_parity_registry.py:24, spec:110, result card:76) is internally refuted by the PR's own CAS-verified identities. I2 (pr182_sympy_axis.py:49-81, fixture TB 3/7->-3/7, EB -2/5->2/5) proves mirror reflection flips both TB and EB, so EB/TB is exactly mirror-invariant (verified numerically on the PR's own fixture: identical sign for model and mirror) — the ratio carries zero handedness information, while the falsifier's comparator (local velocity-curl handedness, registry lines 27-32) is parity-odd. I3's own outputs (n->-n, a->Lambda a) make n2*n3 and a^2 orientation-even, hence h=a^2/(n2 n3)>0 and any x_h from it are orientation-even (sign identically +1 in the standard VII_h convention); repo-wide grep confirms x_h has no definition or signed-handedness convention anywhere. The charitable enumerative reading ('signs of EB and TB', paralleling the pure_boost entry) also fails: it would assert the unproven, l-dependent sign(EB)=sign(TB) and still lacks a signed x_h template. Since the spec and backlog card declare this binding 'the only new sliver', the PR's sole novel contribution is vacuous as registered. P1 (borderline P0) is calibrated correctly: I1-I4 remain valid and no data path exists (FORBIDDEN_PRE_NATIVE), so nothing false ships today, but the registry entry must be re-registered as sign(TB) or sign(EB) individually against a registered signed-handedness convention before commit.
